title: Western P02 tracers reject uniform removal with only recent surface input at 5 percent tolerance in 2013-2022
abstract: We test whether repeated North Pacific CFC-12 and SF6 means can evolve through uniform removal and recent surface input before oxygen is interpreted. At 5 percent independent tracer tolerance, all five western P02 density classes from 26.3 to 26.7 fail, while ten central and eastern classes pass. Independent convex-hull certificates prove each western rejection. On western density 26.5, allowing incoming ages up to 100 years requires at least 3.813 percent older inflow in final mixture mass; a fit must admit water at least 41.34 years old. All 199 spatial block resamples per western class reject recent input. Age-selective removal restores fits with no older inflow, and 10 percent tracer tolerance removes the rejection. These conditional results constrain a local renewal model. They do not identify respiration change, an outcrop share or real inflow. Source saturation, pooled sampling and approximate partial-pressure conservation limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and reproduction instructions are included.

display.caption: Regional tracer rejection thresholds, western older-input bounds, and conditional spatial block ranges under uniform removal. Age-selective removal can fit without older input.
